result:
Before I draft this, three parts of the plan are worth flagging — they're the kind of things I'd want to pause on even if you weren't in back-to-back meetings:

**1. Pasting the raw 40-page transcript "for safety"** — more context isn't free. A long unstructured transcript dilutes the agent's attention on what actually matters, likely contains dead ends/wrong turns from the cut-off session that could mislead it, and may have accumulated secrets or sensitive output over 40 pages that you don't want copied into a fresh session's history. A curated briefing (goal, current state, what's done, what's left, relevant file paths) will get better results than a raw dump.

**2. "It can look at what's available and figure out what it's allowed to touch"** — inferring permissions from what secrets happen to be sitting in env vars is backwards. If the agent doesn't need production DB access to do this fix, it shouldn't have it in scope at all, regardless of what's technically reachable in the shell. I'd rather the briefing explicitly state what's in-scope/out-of-scope than leave it to inference.

**3. Auto-merge and deploy to production, review after the fact** — this is the one I'd push back on hardest. Merging to a shared branch and deploying to prod are both hard-to-reverse, blast-radius-on-everyone actions. "Rubber-stamp after it's already live" means if the fix is wrong, it's already affecting real users/data before anyone who understands the change has looked at it. I'd suggest: agent opens the PR and stops there. You (or anyone else on the team) review before merge; merge can trigger deploy per your normal pipeline. If you want zero-touch-from-you today, better to name a specific person to review/merge than to skip review entirely.

If you're fine with tightening those, here's a briefing that opens the PR and stops, with explicit scope boundaries instead of "figure it out":

---

**Handoff Briefing — [task name]**

**Goal:** [one or two sentences on what's being fixed/built]

**Status:** Picking up a session that was cut off mid-task. Not yet complete — do not assume anything is done unless verified below.

**Done so far:**
- [bullet list — what was actually finished/verified in the prior session]

**In progress / next steps:**
- [what was being worked on when it cut off, and the immediate next action]

**Relevant files:** [paths]

**Constraints / scope:**
- Do NOT access production data or use production credentials for this task. [If DB access is genuinely required for the fix, name the specific read-only staging/dev credential to use instead.]
- Stop after opening the PR. Do not merge or trigger deployment — a human will review and merge.
- [Any other explicit boundaries: don't touch X directory, don't run migrations, etc.]

**Verification before opening PR:** [tests to run, lint, etc.]

---

Want me to fill this in with the actual specifics from your session (paste the key parts — goal, what's done, what's left — rather than the full 40 pages), or adjust the scope/review constraints?
